newsitem.title: INDIA: Federal budget seen vital for India metals trade.
newsitem.headline: Federal budget seen vital for India metals trade.

text.p: Passage of the federal budget for 1997/98 (April/March) is crucial for boosting trade in non-ferrous metals, Bombay Metals Exchange president Sharad Parikh said on Wednesday.
Parikh said government agencies normally placed orders soon after the dudget, which allocates funds for them for the fiscal year.
Parliament began debating the budget this week and it was expected to be passed later this month.
Parikh said changes proposed in import tariffs on non-ferrous metals would also take effect with the passage of the budget.
The budget proposed to double import duty on aluminium ingots to 20 percent to protect the domestic industry.
In the debate on Wednesday, Finance Minister P. Chidambaram said he proposed to cut import duty on ferro-nickel to 10 percent from 20 percent.
Chidambaram said the measure was being taken to provide relief to the steel industry.

State-owned Hindustan Copper Ltd (HCL) and Hindustan Zinc Ltd (HZL) have reduced the May prices of their products by 1,000 rupees per tonne to make them competitive against imports and supplies by local private companies.
Traders said both HCL and HZL reduced their prices despite a firm trend on the London Metals Exchange (LME).
India meets most of its non-ferrous metals requirements through imports, and LME prices have a direct bearing on the local market.
"HCL and HZL should have raised their prices in line with the LME trend but reduced them instead to spur demand," Parikh said. "But demand has yet to pick up."
In the week to Wednesday non-ferrous metals trade was very slow in the absence of buyers.
